title: Introspective canary with sample-weight stabilizer and adaptive smoke thresholds
author: Aisha R. Khan
description:
Context: We see repeated short-lived canary flaps across heterogeneous traffic slices where small sample-size noise causes traffic fraction to oscillate and triggers false-positive rollbacks. This PR introduces an 'introspective canary stabilizer' that maintains statistical power while damping sample-weight oscillations and automatically widening smoke-test windows when variance is high. Motivation: reduce operational churn, avoid unnecessary rollbacks, and keep canaries meaningful for low-volume slices.

What this PR does (high level): Implements a sample-weight stabilizer component in the rollout controller that: 1) maintains a sliding reservoir of recent successful and failed sample outcomes per slice, 2) estimates effective sample variance and computes a damping factor for traffic weight updates, 3) applies an adaptive smoke threshold that increases tolerance under high variance and decays back as confidence accumulates, and 4) exposes metrics and debug traces for postmortem. Also adds a deterministic simulation harness used in unit and integration tests to validate behavior under bursty and adversarial noise patterns.

Implementation notes: New stabilizer service lives under src/rollout/stabilizer.go and is platform-agnostic (pure Go). It integrates into the existing promote/adjust pipeline via a Stabilizer interface with a single Evaluate(ctx, sliceState) -> StabilizedAdvice call. The advice carries a suggested weight delta and a confidence score (internal float) used by the controller. For testing and observability we added telemetry metrics (telemetry/metrics/canary_stability.prom), structured traces (tracing/tag=canary.stabilizer), and a small docs runbook describing expected behaviors and recovery steps (docs/runbooks/canary-stabilizer.md).

Testing and validation: Unit tests for edge cases (zero samples, perfect consistency, adversarial flips) are in pkg/rollout/stabilizer_test.go. We added simulated e2e scenarios in integration-tests/canary_e2e.yaml that previously caused flaps; the new stabilizer reduces reverts by ~72% in our synthetic replay harness. CI initially flagged an intermittent e2e smoke test; the test was flaky due to timing in the harness and was stabilized with a deterministic clock in the simulator.

Backward compatibility and rollout: The stabilizer is feature-flagged (rollout.introspective_stabilizer), default-off for Dedicated/Private until we finish a short canary in prod. Flag can be toggled per-tenant via rollout config. No API changes to external client-facing surfaces.

Checklist:
- [x] Design doc linked (Linear: ENG-7892)
- [x] Unit tests added
- [x] Integration simulation added
- [x] Telemetry & tracing hooks
- [x] Runbook and release notes

Related: ENG-7892, ENG-8010; support ticket SUP-1345 noted repeated flaps in two customer clusters.

Notes for reviewers: focus on the Stabilizer.Evaluate contract and the damping constant defaults in stabilizer/config.go. The simulation harness is intentionally simplified — it's deterministic by design for reproducible CI runs.

review_comments: Sana Patel: High level LGTM. Please call out in the runbook the expected magnitude of weight dampening for 95% CI so on-call engineers know when to intervene.
Author (Aisha): Added a small note in docs/runbooks/canary-stabilizer.md and left an example table of dampening values for 90/95/99% confidence windows.

release_notes:
- Add introspective canary stabilizer that reduces noise-driven rollbacks and smooths traffic adjustments
- New deterministic simulation harness for validating canary stability under noisy conditions
- Telemetry to track weight drift, deferred updates, and stabilizer confidence
- Feature-flag rollout (rollout.introspective_stabilizer) - default off for Dedicated/Private
